summary:
Technical review of rework-4 (sub-mv3t8kff-017759bd: migration 006, the fail-open general limiter, the access-hook wiring and six test files, plus the submission), against the resolution conditions of TR-D-3 (phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56) and SEC-R-1 (rework-1 review). The security draft rework-4-security-1.md (FINAL) is folded in with its ids.

Decision: changes requested, for one major finding, SEC-RW4-1. The security reviewer rates it minor; I raise it to major, with my own reproduction.
- **What goes wrong:** 006 seeds sqlite_sequence from the highest id that survives. Ids hard-deleted on 005 above that id are handed out again after the upgrade, while audit_events and model_spend still name them.
- **My reproduction (ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00):** X deletes request 2 with image 11, run 101 and plan version 30 on 005. After 006, Y's next rows get exactly 2/11/101/30, and 2 of X's audit rows sit on Y's request id. With the security reviewer's ~10 lines of sequence statements, the next ids are 3/12/102/31, the FK and integrity checks are clean, and the rows are unchanged.
- **Why major:** the rebuild exists for databases that already hold data, and on exactly those the condition 'ids never reused' fails. It can be repaired only before 006 is applied anywhere: NFR1 refuses an edit afterwards, and a 007 cannot take back ids already handed out. The rework limit is used, so a change after approval would need a fifth rework from the user. Now it is a reset of this task.

Everything else holds.

Declared checks:
- Green set: 120/120 (ev:ev-mv3teu8p-01309af2).
- npm test, runs 1 and 2: 2055 tests, 2039 pass, 1 fail, 15 skipped each. The one failure is e6's known route-table row (ev:ev-mv3tgz6r-011bfe69, ev:ev-mv3tiyy9-01f99271).
- npm test, run 3, through a known-failure filter, after e4's final commit: 2062 tests, 2054 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped, ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 (ev:ev-mv3u0bm4-018df267).
- npm run test:browser: 8/8 (ev:ev-mv3tj9bo-01e55981).

My own checks:
- Falsification (ev:ev-mv3toj9i-01cfede3): the control is green, 87/87. The pre-rework source fails 7 of 14. All 13 mutants are killed: 6 on the migration, 5 on the limiter, 1 on the hook.
- Probes (ev:ev-mv3tp49m-017879bb): SEC-R-1 end to end through createApp, and 006 on a seeded WAL file database (all 3454 rows equal; schema equal to a fresh one).
- Migration cost (ev:ev-mv3tpe9a-016d484a). Coverage: 9 declared, 9 changed, 9 submitted (ev:ev-mv3tps3r-01befc44). sha256 of the artifacts unchanged (ev:ev-mv3tpsb0-01a2c0fe).

SEC-R-1 is resolved. The other findings are minor or info: TR-R4-1..TR-R4-4 and TR-R4-6..TR-R4-9, and SEC-RW4-I1..I5. TR-R4-5 is merged into SEC-RW4-I2.

criteria.description: FU-23 and SEC-R-1: ids never reused; general limit fails open on busy reads

Phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56 TR-D-3 and security draft: rescue_requests, plan_versions, images and planning_runs use INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after a hard delete of the highest id the next row reuses it and audit rows or a model_spend row point at another customer's request; migration 006 rebuilds those tables with AUTOINCREMENT (app-only, data preserved), model_spend.request_id gets a foreign key or check, and an RS-39 test shows no id is reused. Rework-1 review SEC-R-1: src/auth/general-limit.js takes the write lock on every signed-in call; GET and HEAD fail open on a busy error (the request proceeds uncounted and the event is logged), with a lock-holder test. Only b1 and c1 (approved) owned these files. Required before e4.
criteria.notes:
Not met: on an upgraded database, the next row takes over an id that was hard-deleted before the upgrade, and that id's audit rows then point at another customer's request. That is the very harm the condition names, and it is reproduced in ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00 and ev:ev-mv3twi5f-015c7a17.

The safety argument's point 6 ('a deleted highest id is never handed out again') holds only for deletes made after the upgrade.

What is met:
- The existing checks pass (run 3 is green).
- The scope extension was justified.
- The record of the refused second handoff is complete (TR-R4-7).
- 'Before e4': e4 was built in parallel (TR-R4-8).

criteria.description: The rework's not-applicable decision on mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 holds
criteria.notes: The lesson applies to hooks or guards that map file writes to a project record or root. The rework's nine files are a SQL migration, the application's rate limiter and access hook, and tests. None of them is a tool-call guard, a pre-commit hook or root discovery. Not applicable.

findings.title: Migration 006 hands out again ids that were hard-deleted before the upgrade, so FU-23's cross-customer audit mix-up reappears on every upgraded database
findings.detail:
006 re-inserts the surviving rows, which sets each sqlite_sequence to max(id) of the survivors (comment at L20: 'the best high-water mark that is known'). Higher ids are known, though:
- audit_events.entity_id (request, image, plan_version);
- audit_events.detail_json of plan.create (planVersionId, runId);
- the staged model_spend.request_id.

Reproduction:
- Mine (ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00): X hard-deletes request 2 (image 11, run 101, plan version 30) on 005. After 006, Y's next request, image, run and plan version get 2/11/101/30, and 2 of X's audit rows name Y's request id.
- The security reviewer's, through the real HTTP flows (ev:ev-mv3twi5f-015c7a17): Y gets request 5 and image 4, and the admin timeline of Y's request lists X's request.create, extraction.run and request.delete. It also reproduces in isolation (ev:ev-mv3u2o6u-0130d038).

The proposed statements raise each sequence to the highest named id before the staging tables are dropped. With them the next ids are 3/12/102/31, the FK and integrity checks are clean and the rows are unchanged; both reviewers ran this.

Severity: security rates it minor, like the original FU-23. I raise it to major for three reasons.
1. It defeats the rework's own condition ('an RS-39 test shows no id is reused') on the databases the rebuild exists for.
2. It becomes irreversible as soon as 006 is applied to a persistent database: NFR1 refuses an edit, and a 007 cannot reclaim ids already reissued.
3. The rework limit is used, so after approval the only route is a fifth rework from the user, whereas now it is a reset of this task.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, after the orchestrator resets rework-4. Resolved when all of the following hold:
- 006, before it drops the staging tables, creates any missing sqlite_sequence row and raises each rebuilt table's sequence to the maximum of its surviving ids and every id still named. For rescue_requests that means audit request entity ids and the staged model_spend.request_id; for images, audit image entity ids; for plan_versions, audit plan_version entity ids and plan.create detail planVersionId; for planning_runs, plan.create detail runId. The statements in rework-4-security-1.md are acceptable.
- The comment at L20 and safety-argument point 6 are corrected.
- A new test (named RS-39) deletes the highest request, image, run and plan version on 005 before migrating, and asserts that none of those ids is handed out afterwards and that no earlier audit row names the new rows. It must be recorded failing on the submitted 006 and passing on the fixed one.
- The existing migrate-006 assertions are kept, with the sequence expectation updated to the new high-water mark.
- The green set, npm test and the browser suite pass.

findings.title: Migration 006's run time grows quadratically with the number of plan versions: about 9 s at 5000 request trees, holding the write lock
findings.detail:
Measured on scratch file databases, with 2 plan versions per tree and every 5th tree also holding a reservation and a supplier order:
- 1000 trees: 0.27-0.35 s.
- 2000 trees: 1.1 s.
- 4000 trees: 5.3 s.
- 5000 trees: 8.7 s.
(ev:ev-mv3tpe9a-016d484a; ev:ev-mv3tp49m-017879bb P3)

Nearly all of the time is in DROP TABLE plan_versions and INSERT INTO plan_versions. That fits the deferred-FK child scans over columns that have no index: plan_versions.superseded_by, reservations.plan_version_id and supplier_orders.plan_version_id.

The submission describes this cost as linear; it is not. Beyond about 4000 trees, a second process starting at the same time would hit its 5 s busy timeout. This is irrelevant at the demo's scale.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer in the same reset (optional), else the orchestrator. Resolved when either of these holds:
- 006 adds temporary indexes on plan_versions(superseded_by), reservations(plan_version_id) and supplier_orders(plan_version_id) and drops them before the end, so the schema stays identical, and a re-measurement shows near-linear growth.
- The operator note and the verification report state the measured cost and that one process upgrades before traffic.

findings.title: SEC-R-1 has no committed HTTP-level test; HEAD answers 405 through the router
findings.detail: The limiter unit test uses a real lock-holder process, and the hook test uses a mock. Both are mutant-tested. My P1 probe covers the HTTP path: GET 200 in 54 ms, one busy_open line, POST 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1. HEAD never reaches the hook, because the router answers 405 first; the security reviewer confirms this.
findings.recommendation: Owner: optional, the next src/auth or test/api touch. Resolved when an API test shows GET 200 and POST 503 under a held lock through createApp, or the orchestrator records that the unit tests plus the probes suffice.

findings.title: Pre-existing: a state-changing call waiting for a lock held by another process stalls the whole process for RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS
findings.detail: In my P4 probe, a 100 ms timer set right after a signed-in POST fired at 5015 ms, while the POST waited for 503. The busy wait of node:sqlite is synchronous. The read fail-open therefore helps only while no write of the same process waits. SEC-RW4-I4 is the same class, for the session touch.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the phase E reviewers and the orchestrator. Resolved when the phase E review confirms that reconciler and saga transactions are short (no await inside db.tx) and the verification report lists the residual; or a later rework shortens the write wait for request handlers.

findings.title: TR-D-3's report wording is superseded: model_spend rows of a hard-deleted request keep the row and lose the pointer (SET NULL)
findings.detail: After 006 the spend row survives with request_id NULL, and the daily sums are unchanged (my id-reuse run, and the security reviewer's metrics check). Dangling pointers that existed before the upgrade are set to NULL by 006; P2 found 43 of them.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator (verification report). Resolved when the report states the SET NULL behaviour and the NULLing at the upgrade.

findings.title: The uploads-retention startApp timer test is a flaky test race and not a rework-4 effect; it recurred in the security reviewer's run
findings.detail:
The test polls until the image row is gone, then asserts the file is gone at once. The sweep unlinks only after its commit, so the test can catch the moment in between.
- It failed in ev:ev-mv3t54i6-01a9b844 and ev:ev-mv3tzf4g-0111832e.
- It passed in my three full runs and alone (ev:ev-mv3tzro0-016ab924).
No rework-4 file is on this path.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator routes it to the owner of test/api/uploads-retention.test.js. Resolved when the test also waits for the file's absence, and three consecutive npm test runs are green on that row.

findings.title: The refused second handoff: the record is complete through both handoffs; the engine gap is TK-5
findings.detail: The orchestrator's snapshot commit 507da7e became the second claim's base, so the engine refused its full file list. The two handoffs together declare all nine files, and my coverage check finds 9 declared, 9 changed, 9 submitted and 0 undeclared. That suffices.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the ECCode toolkit (TK-5). Resolved when completion compares against the task's first claim base, or snapshot commits stop rebasing an active claim. The resubmission's handoff should again declare every file it changes.

findings.title: e4 was built and completed in parallel with this rework, against dec-mv39rg82-01a682bc and my TR-D-3 ordering
findings.detail: e4-saga-reconciler is done (a08aac7). It owns none of this rework's files, and run 3 is green with e4's final code. The ordering's protection holds only if phase:e-payments is approved after this gate.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator. Resolved when phase:e-payments is approved only after phase:rework-4, and the decision log records the change of ordering.

findings.title: Toolkit defect: tree pinning is off in this nested project whenever any file is dirty
findings.detail: lib/project.js treeDigest() passes paths stripped of the project prefix to git hash-object --stdin-paths with the project as cwd. git resolves them from the repository root and fails, so the digest is null. The .eccode record files are always dirty between commits, so cited checks are not bound to a tree, and the engine's stale-check silently skips them (ev:ev-mv3u16vc-014dd303).
findings.recommendation: Owner: the ECCode toolkit (file as a TK item; dispatch learning-debugger only if the cause is disputed). Resolved when treeDigest hashes dirty files by paths git resolves correctly, with a regression test: in a project below the repository root, one modified tracked file and one untracked file give a non-null digest that changes with either file.

findings.title: (security) extractions and requirements ids are still reused after a hard delete
findings.detail: From the security draft. Y's request view and X's audit detail can both carry extractionId 1. No route looks anything up by these ids, and the timeline does not mix them. I agree the condition named only the four tables.
findings.recommendation: Owner: backend-engineer, optional in the same reset (both tables are already staged). Resolved when they get AUTOINCREMENT with the same sequence rule as SEC-RW4-1, or the orchestrator records them as accepted.

findings.title: (security; merges TR-R4-5) an extract racing a hard delete of the same request now answers 500 INTERNAL instead of 404
findings.detail: The security reviewer ran the race 25 times, with the same result each time. The new FK refuses reserve's insert, and toAppError maps it to 500. No provider call or spend row results, which is better than before, when the paid call happened first. My code reading agrees: extractRequest awaits loadImageForModel between the owner check and gate.run.
findings.recommendation: Owner: optional, the next touch of src/services/extraction.js or src/ai/gate.js. Resolved when an FK failure at reserve maps to 404 NOT_FOUND (or the owner is re-checked inside the reserve transaction) with a test, or the orchestrator records it as accepted.

findings.title: (security) the read fail-open allows uncounted reads only while another connection holds the lock; a user cannot cause it
findings.detail: From the security draft. 40 concurrent writes plus 120 reads by one user were all counted, with no busy_open line, because the app uses a single synchronous connection. While the lock was held, reads throttled the process to about 18 per second. Accepted by design.
findings.recommendation: No action. Resolved by this record.

findings.title: (security, outside this diff) the session touch on a GET still waits the full busy timeout synchronously
findings.detail: From the security draft. A GET took 1057 ms under a held lock with a 1000 ms busy timeout (src/auth/sessions.js, the touch UPDATE). This is the same class as TR-R4-3.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the next src/auth touch. Resolved when the touch uses the short wait or skips on busy, with a lock-holder test; or the orchestrator records it as accepted.

findings.title: (security) collisions made before 006 stay as they are
findings.detail: Confirmed on a 005 database filled through the app: a model_spend row naming a reused id is unchanged after 006. This cannot be repaired from the data, and the submission discloses it.
findings.recommendation: No action. Resolved by this record.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Condition met.
- take() fails open only for GET and HEAD and only on a busy error, uncounted, with one rate_limit.busy_open line that carries the request id only.
- Reads wait at most 50 ms, and the timeout is restored.
- State-changing methods, and a call with no method, fail closed with 503 DB_BUSY.
- The hook passes req.method, which cannot be spoofed: there is no override header or parameter, as the security reviewer confirmed.
- Through createApp, a signed-in GET answers 200 under a held lock and a POST answers 503 (P1).
- The pre-rework limiter fails the lock-holder tests, and all limiter and hook mutants are killed.
The change to 006 that SEC-RW4-1 requires does not touch these files.
